question: Compare how the Transformer and LLaMA encode word positions.

expected.attention is all you need: sinusoidal positional encodings: sine and cosine functions of different frequencies added to the embeddings
expected.llm paper (1): rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) at each layer instead of absolute positional embeddings

attention is all you need: we use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies
llm paper (1): we remove the absolute positional embeddings

question: Compare the activation functions used in BERT and LLaMA.

bert: we use a gelu acti- vation
llm paper (1): we re- place the relu non-linearity by the swiglu

question: Compare the normalization used in the Transformer and LLaMA.

expected.attention is all you need: layer normalization applied after each sub-layer with a residual connection: LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x))
expected.llm paper (1): pre-normalization: RMSNorm applied to the input of each sub-layer

llm paper (1): we use the rmsnorm normalizing func- tion

question: Compare the optimizer and learning-rate schedule of the Transformer and LLaMA.

expected.attention is all you need: Adam (beta1 0.9, beta2 0.98) with a learning rate that increases linearly during warmup and then decreases with the inverse square root of the step number
expected.llm paper (1): AdamW (beta1 0.9, beta2 0.95) with a cosine learning rate schedule ending at 10% of the maximum

attention is all you need: varied the learning rate over the course of training
llm paper (1): we use a cosine learning rate schedule

question: Compare the pre-training data of BERT and LLaMA.

expected.bert: BooksCorpus (800M words) and English Wikipedia (2,500M words)
expected.llm paper (1): a mixture of publicly available data, mostly English CommonCrawl (67%), about 1.4T tokens in total

question: Compare the overall architecture of the Transformer and BERT.

expected.attention is all you need: an encoder-decoder structure, with stacks of N = 6 identical layers
expected.bert: a multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder (encoder only)

question: Compare the hardware used to train the Transformer, BERT and LLaMA.

expected.attention is all you need: one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs
expected.bert: Cloud TPUs: 4 Cloud TPUs (16 TPU chips) for BERT-base, 16 Cloud TPUs for BERT-large

question: Give a full comparison of BERT and LLaMA.

expected.bert: goal: pre-train deep bidirectional representations (masked LM + next sentence prediction) for fine-tuning; strong results such as GLUE 80.5%
expected.llm paper (1): goal: foundation language models from 7B to 65B trained only on public data; LLaMA-13B outperforms GPT-3 on most benchmarks
